minutes.headline: Four wetland-permit hearings were continued over disputed boundary flagging amid an understaffed conservation office
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission approved Hickory Hills Lake's annual fanwort herbicide treatment plan, but continued four separate wetland-permit hearings (417 and 390 Howard Street, 31 Round Road, 221 Electric Ave) to June 4 after commissioners repeatedly could not confirm wetland flagging or delineation reports, and redirected a restaurant patio project from an administrative determination to a full RDA filing. Much of the meeting also concerned staffing and records gaps left by a departed conservation agent/assistant — missing budget reports, an incomplete Google Drive-to-SharePoint migration, and enforcement cases awaiting follow-up from a part-time interim administrator.

what_happened.line: Four wetland-permit hearings (417 and 390 Howard Street, 31 Round Road, 221 Electric Ave) were continued to June 4 after commissioners could not confirm boundary flagging or delineation reports.
No monthly budget report has reached the commission since the prior conservation agent/assistant departed, and the shift of records from Google Drive to SharePoint remains incomplete.
A restaurant patio and wall project at 5 Electric Ave was redirected from an administrative determination to a full Request for Determination of Applicability filing.
The commission approved the annual fanwort herbicide treatment plan for Hickory Hills Lake.
Commissioners asked the interim administrator to pursue additional state resources for the long-standing wetland alteration violation at 1168 Mass Ave rear.

why_it_matters: Residents with pending applications on Howard Street, Round Road, and Electric Ave face a further wait, with those hearings now pushed to June 4.
